senses.definition: (slang) To tire out or exhaust a person or animal.
examples: Man, I’m so tuckered from my run today.

senses.definition: (countable) One who or that which tucks.
examples:
Discrimination. Firm, after having had a long controversy with its tuckers, laid off the whole tucking department for a week. Union maintained it was a clear case cf discrimination against the tuckers on account of the recent controversy.
Determination:
Complaint of the union was sustained. Tuckers were paid the amount of money they were deprived of through being discriminated against, $158.90.

senses.definition: (uncountable, colloquial, Australia, New Zealand) Food; tuck.

quotes.text: By the fire the billies were boiling, the tucker of both camps spread out on tarpaulins.

senses.definition: (slang, dated) Work that scarcely yields a living wage.
(countable) Lace or a piece of cloth in the neckline of a dress.

quotes.text:
“And, ma′am,” he continued, “the laundress tells me some of the girls have two clean tuckers in the week: it is too much; the rules limit them to one.”
